openalex_record.title: Preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma with a radiological feature-based nomogram: a bi-centre study
openalex_record.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a nomogram for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on the radiological features of enhanced CT and to verify two imaging techniques (CT and MRI) in an external centre. METHOD: A total of 346 patients were retrospectively included (training, n = 185, CT images; external testing 1, n = 90, CT images; external testing 2, n = 71, MRI images), including 229 MVI-negative patients and 117 MVI-positive patients. The radiological features and clinical information of enhanced CT images were analysed, and the independent variables associated with MVI in HCC were determined by logistic regression analysis. Then, a nomogram prediction model was constructed. External validation was performed on CT (n = 90) and MRI (n = 71) images from another centre. RESULTS: Among the 23 radiological and clinical features, size, arterial peritumoral enhancement (APE), tumour margin and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) were independent influencing factors for MVI in HCC. The nomogram integrating these risk factors had a good predictive effect, with AUC, specificity and sensitivity values of 0.834 (95% CI: 0.774-0.895), 75.0% and 83.5%, respectively. The AUC values of external verification based on CT and MRI image data were 0.794 (95% CI: 0.700-0.888) and 0.883 (95% CI: 0.807-0.959), respectively. No statistical difference in AUC values among training set and testing sets was found. CONCLUSION: The proposed nomogram prediction model for MVI in HCC has high accuracy, can be used with different imaging techniques, and has good clinical applicability.

fulltext.text: CE-CT scanning of the liver was performed using multiple multislice spiral CT scanners. Scan from the roof of the diaphragm to the iliac ridge. It includes plain scan, arterial stage (fluoroscopic trigger, 28 ~ 35 s), portal vein stage (70-80 s) and equilibrium stage (180 s). All patients received a non-ionic iodide contrast (300 mg of iodide per ml) at a dose of 1.5 ml (450 mg of iodide) per kg of body weight with a flow rate of 3.0–4.0 ml/s. Detailed imaging parameters of CT are shown in Table 1.

fulltext.text: Overall, 346 consecutive patients (185 patients from Centre I and 161 patients from Centre II) were enrolled, and the CT imaging data from Centre I were set as a training cohort. records.title: Preoperative prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma microvascular invasion based on magnetic resonance imaging feature extraction artificial neural network
records.abstract: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence is highly correlated with increased mortality. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is indicative of aggressive tumor biology in HCC. AIM To construct an artificial neural network (ANN) capable of accurately predicting MVI presence in HCC using magnetic resonance imaging. METHODS This study included 255 patients with HCC with tumors < 3 cm. Radiologists annotated the tumors on the T1-weighted plain MR images. Subsequently, a three-layer ANN was constructed using image features as inputs to predict MVI status in patients with HCC. Postoperative pathological examination is considered the gold standard for determining MVI. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to evaluate the effectiveness of the algorithm. RESULTS Using the bagging strategy to vote for 50 classifier classification results, a prediction model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.79. Moreover, correlation analysis revealed that alpha-fetoprotein values and tumor volume were not significantly correlated with the occurrence of MVI, whereas tumor sphericity was significantly correlated with MVI (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION Analysis of variable correlations regarding MVI in tumors with diameters < 3 cm should prioritize tumor sphericity. The ANN model demonstrated strong predictive MVI for patients with HCC (AUC = 0.79).

records.title: Deep Neural Network and Radiomics-based Magnetic Resonance Imaging System for Predicting Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
records.abstract: Background: Accurate preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is crucial for surgeons to make informed decisions regarding appropriate treatment strategies.However, it continues to pose a significant challenge for radiologists.The integration of computer-aided diagnosis utilizing deep learning technology emerges as a promising approach to enhance the prediction accuracy.Methods: This experiment incorporated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans with six different sequences.After a cross-sequence registration preprocess, a deep neural network was employed for the segmentation of hepatocellular carcinoma.The final prediction model was constructed by combining radiomics features with clinical features.The selection of clinical features for the final model was determined through univariate analysis.Results: In this study, we analyzed MRI scans obtained from a cohort of 420 patients diagnosed with HCC.Among them, 140 cases exhibited MVI, while the remaining 280 cases comprised the non-MVI group.The radiomics features demonstrated strong predictive capability for MVI.By extracting radiomic features from each MRI sequence and subsequently integrating them, we achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.794±0.033.Specifically, for tumor sizes ranging from 3 to 5 cm, the AUC reached 0.860±0.065.Conclusions: In this study, we present a fully automatic system for predicting MVI in HCC based on preoperative MRI.Our approach leverages the fusion of radiomics and clinical features to achieve accurate MVI prediction.The system demonstrates robust performance in predicting MVI, particularly in the 3-5 cm tumor group.

records.title: Radiogenomics nomogram based on MRI and microRNAs to predict microvascular invasion of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to develop and validate a radiogenomics nomogram for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) on the basis of MRI and microRNAs (miRNAs). Materials and methods: This cohort study included 168 patients (training cohort: n = 116; validation cohort: n = 52) with pathologically confirmed HCC, who underwent preoperative MRI and plasma miRNA examination. Univariate and multivariate logistic regressions were used to identify independent risk factors associated with MVI. These risk factors were used to produce a nomogram. The performance of the nomogram was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis was performed to determine whether the nomogram was clinically useful. Results: The independent risk factors for MVI were maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21 (all P < 0.001). The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score of the nomogram in the validation cohort were 0.970, 0.722, 0.884, and 0.916, respectively. The AUC of the nomogram was 0.900 (95% CI: 0.808-0.992) in the validation cohort, higher than that of any other single factor model (maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21). Conclusion: The radiogenomics nomogram shows satisfactory predictive performance in predicting MVI in HCC and provides a feasible and practical reference for tumor treatment decisions.

records.title: Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma and Its Prognostic Implications: A Multicenter Study
records.abstract: Introduction: Previous studies on preoperative predictors of microvascular invasion (MVI) in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICCA) have presented inconsistent results. This study aimed to identify preoperative clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) factors that can predict MVI in ICCA and to evaluate their prognostic utility using a multicenter cohort. Methods: A multicenter cohort of 446 patients who underwent preoperative MRI and surgical resection for ICCA at six tertiary referral institutions between 2009 and 2018 was analyzed for clinical, pathologic, and MR imaging characteristics. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify significant predictors of pathologically confirmed MVI, which were subsequently used to stratify patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups based on the number of predictors identified. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and log-rank test were conducted to assess long-term survival and early recurrence among the three groups. Results: Among the 446 patients (mean age, 63.0 ± 9.9 years; 277 men), 234 (52.5%) had MVI on pathology. Independent predictors of MVI included serum carbohydrate antigen 19–9 levels (≥80 U/mL; odds ratio [OR]: 2.68, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.64–4.37, p < 0.001), tumor size (≥4 cm; OR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.01–2.54, p = 0.046), tumor multiplicity (OR: 2.84, 95% CI: 1.58–5.12, p < 0.001), and arterial phase peritumoral enhancement (OR: 2.83, 95% CI: 1.81–4.42, p < 0.001). Stratifying patients by MVI risk – low (no predictors), intermediate (1–3 predictors), and high (4 predictors) – revealed a significant decrease in both recurrence-free and overall survival rates (p < 0.001), along with a corresponding increase in early recurrence rates (p < 0.001) as the risk level increased. Conclusion: Risk stratification utilizing four key predictors can effectively assess the risk of MVI in ICCA and is associated with postoperative outcomes.

records.title: Interpretable and generalizable deep learning model for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion and outcome in hepatocellular carcinoma based on MRI: a multicenter study
records.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop an interpretable, domain-generalizable deep learning model for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). METHODS: Utilizing a retrospective dataset of 546 HCC patients from five centers, we developed and validated a clinical-radiological model and deep learning models aimed at MVI prediction. The models were developed on a dataset of 263 cases consisting of data from three centers, internally validated on a set of 66 patients, and externally tested on two independent sets. An adversarial network-based deep learning (AD-DL) model was developed to learn domain-invariant features from multiple centers within the training set. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated using pathological MVI status. With the best-performed model, early recurrence-free survival (ERFS) stratification was validated on the external test set by the log-rank test, and the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with MVI status were tested on the RNA sequencing analysis of the Cancer Imaging Archive. RESULTS: The AD-DL model demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance and generalizability with an AUC of 0.793 in the internal test set, 0.801 in external test set 1, and 0.773 in external test set 2. The model's prediction of MVI status also demonstrated a significant correlation with ERFS (p = 0.048). DEGs associated with MVI status were primarily enriched in the metabolic processes and the Wnt signaling pathway, and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition process. CONCLUSIONS: The AD-DL model allows preoperative MVI prediction and ERFS stratification in HCC patients, which has a good generalizability and biological interpretability. CRITICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: The adversarial network-based deep learning model predicts MVI status well in HCC patients and demonstrates good generalizability. By integrating bioinformatics analysis of the model's predictions, it achieves biological interpretability, facilitating its clinical translation. KEY POINTS: Current MVI assessment models for HCC lack interpretability and generalizability. The adversarial network-based model's performance surpassed clinical radiology and squeeze-and-excitation network-based models. Biological function analysis was employed to enhance the interpretability and clinical translatability of the adversarial network-based model.

records.title: Preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma with a radiological feature-based nomogram: a bi-centre study
records.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a nomogram for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on the radiological features of enhanced CT and to verify two imaging techniques (CT and MRI) in an external centre. METHOD: A total of 346 patients were retrospectively included (training, n = 185, CT images; external testing 1, n = 90, CT images; external testing 2, n = 71, MRI images), including 229 MVI-negative patients and 117 MVI-positive patients. The radiological features and clinical information of enhanced CT images were analysed, and the independent variables associated with MVI in HCC were determined by logistic regression analysis. Then, a nomogram prediction model was constructed. External validation was performed on CT (n = 90) and MRI (n = 71) images from another centre. RESULTS: Among the 23 radiological and clinical features, size, arterial peritumoral enhancement (APE), tumour margin and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) were independent influencing factors for MVI in HCC. The nomogram integrating these risk factors had a good predictive effect, with AUC, specificity and sensitivity values of 0.834 (95% CI: 0.774-0.895), 75.0% and 83.5%, respectively. The AUC values of external verification based on CT and MRI image data were 0.794 (95% CI: 0.700-0.888) and 0.883 (95% CI: 0.807-0.959), respectively. No statistical difference in AUC values among training set and testing sets was found. CONCLUSION: The proposed nomogram prediction model for MVI in HCC has high accuracy, can be used with different imaging techniques, and has good clinical applicability.

records.title: Accuracy of artificial intelligence models integrating machine learning and deep learning in detecting microvascular invasion in liver cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.abstract: e16184 Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a global health challenge, ranking sixth in incidence and third in cancer-related mortality. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a crucial prognostic marker influencing recurrence rates and survival. Accurate preoperative MVI detection can guide surgical planning but is limited by invasive histopathological exams and interobserver variability. This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), in predicting MVI in HCC using imaging modalities such as CT, MRI, ultrasound, PET/CT, and histopathology. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines, covering studies from 2010 to 2023. Comprehensive searches were conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, European PMC, and BioMed Central. AI models were assessed for diagnostic accuracy using QUADAS-2 and Radiomics Quality Score (RQS). Metrics like the area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity were analyzed. Results: This meta-analysis synthesized data from 51 studies, encompassing 6,257 records. DL models showed a pooled AUC of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.80–0.86), with sensitivity and specificity of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75–0.82) and 0.84 (95% CI: 0.79–0.88), respectively. ML models achieved a pooled AUC of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.80–0.86), sensitivity of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.71–0.85), and higher specificity of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.84–0.92). Across imaging modalities, MRI and CT-based models achieved pooled AUCs of 0.87 and 0.83 for DL and 0.85 and 0.82 for ML, respectively. Ultrasound-based models demonstrated higher specificity but slightly lower sensitivity. Models incorporating clinical features did not outperform purely radiomics-based approaches. Quality assessments revealed low bias risks in patient selection (88%), index tests (94%), and reference standards (98%). However, only 51% of studies addressed inter-scanner variability, and 55% incorporated calibration or resampling. The mean RQS was 40%, with 84% adhering to robust imaging protocols. Conclusions: AI models, particularly DL, exhibit robust accuracy in predicting MVI in HCC, showing promise for integration into clinical workflows. These tools could enable personalized preoperative planning, improving patient outcomes and reducing recurrence risks. Standardized protocols, prospective validation, and broader adoption of advanced AI methods are needed to ensure consistent clinical utility and cost-effectiveness.

records.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI deep learning model combined with clinical model for noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
records.abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). Methods The internal development cohort comprised 334 surgically confirmed patients, including 231 patients with HCC and 103 with MF-ICC, and was divided at the patient level into a training cohort ( n = 233) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 101). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. Moreover, a clinical model was built based on independent predictors identified through multivariate analysis, which was ultimately integrated with the best-performing deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated and compared. Results Deep learning model directly feeding the three-phase images as a multi-channel input achieved better discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.814 in the internal validation cohort) than all single-phase and corresponding fusion models. The comprehensive 2D + multi-channel + clinical model showed the best performance for the differentiation of HCC from MF-ICC, achieving an AUC of 0.887 (95% CI, 0.819–0.954) in the internal validation cohort, and generalized well to the external validation cohort (AUC = 0.908; 95% CI, 0.811–1.000). However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.

records.title: LIVER CANCER DETECTION USING RESNET, SWIN TRANSFORMER AND CONVNEXT TINY NETWORKS
records.journal: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
records.abstract: Liver tumor detection from CT images is challenging because most CT slices do not contain tumors, while only a small number contain tumor regions. Another challenge is that slices from the same patient can be very similar, which may cause data leakage when splitting the data randomly. This study focuses on classifying liver CT slices into Tumor and No-Tumor classes using deep learning. The LiTS and 3Dircadb datasets are combined and used for the experiments. Three deep learning models, Swin-T, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet-50, are trained and evaluated. A patient-level data split is used to keep patients in the training, validation, and test sets separate. The three models are also combined using a soft-voting ensemble. The final evaluation is performed on an unseen test set containing 6,323 slices. The soft-voting ensemble achieved the highest accuracy of 92.74%. These results show that the models can detect tumor and no-tumor slices, while the class imbalance remains an important challenge for tumor detection.

records.title: Preoperative prediction of HCC microvascular invasion by multimodel peritumoral diffusion MRI
records.abstract: Abstract Objective Most studies emphasize intratumoral diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics, but few studies have examined whether peritumoral DWI metrics can provide added value. We aimed to evaluate three-dimensional, multiscale, multimodel DWI parameters within intratumoral and peritumoral volumes of interest for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Materials and methods Seventy patients with HCC, including 42 with MVI, were prospectively enrolled. We calculated parameters from monoexponential, intravoxel incoherent motion, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched-exponential model (SEM), and continuous-time random-walk models within the tumor and in 3-mm (P3) and 5-mm (P5) peritumoral rims. Features showing differences on univariable analysis were further screened using logistic regression with variance inflation factor filtering to build combined models. Diagnostic performance was assessed by areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results Four intratumoral diffusion-coefficient–related metrics showed significant differences between groups. In the peritumoral regions, 12 parameters differed between groups, including diffusion-coefficient–related indices and heterogeneity-related metrics. Among single parameters, P3_DKI_ K app achieved the best discrimination for MVI (AUROC = 0.713); P5_DKI_ K app and Tumor_SEM_DDC were selected as independent imaging predictors. After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_ K app , and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Conclusion Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Key Points Question Can multiscale, multimodel peritumoral DWI metrics improve preoperative prediction of MVI in HCC compared with intratumoral DWI metrics? Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

records.title: Preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in small hepatocellular carcinoma (≤ 3 cm) by leveraging cross-phase variations of MRI contrast phases
records.abstract: Abstract Purpose Noninvasive preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a significant clinical challenge worldwide. This study encoded feature variations across multi-phase MRI sequences for the preoperative prediction of MVI. Method Data were retrospectively examined for 115 consecutive patients (mean age: 57.2 ± 10.7 years; 95 men) who had undergone surgical resection for HCC (tumor diameter less than 3 cm). All of them underwent preoperative MR examination and were randomly partitioned into training and testing cohorts at an 8:2 ratio. Peritumoral expansions (3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm) were generated from manually segmented intratumoral regions of interest (ROIs) across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases. Radiomics features were subsequently extracted from both the original and expanded ROIs. We then evaluated the predictive performance of five encoding methods combined with four machine learning classifiers using both clinical characteristics and radiomics features. Result Multi-phase models incorporating temporal encoding methods consistently outperformed single-phase models and those relying solely on clinical characteristics. Among all evaluated combinations, the Fourier-inspired temporal encoding method combined with an ExtraTrees classifier, applied to the original tumoral ROI with a 5-mm peritumoral expansion, achieved the best diagnostic performance, with an AUC of 0.850 (95% CI: 0.675–0.978). Conclusion While radiologists routinely monitor multi-phase contrast dynamics qualitatively, our findings demonstrate that these cross-phase variations provide quantifiable, highly predictive information for MVI. This framework represents a promising, noninvasive quantitative tool for preoperative MVI risk stratification.

records.title: A multiparametric liver MRI dataset with multiple tumor and liver segmentations of pre-treatment hepatocellular carcinomas
records.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) plays a key role for HCC screening, diagnosis and treatment planning, the development of AI models for detection and characterization of focal liver lesions is hindered by the scarcity of publicly available annotated MRI datasets. Here, we present OpenSwissHCC, a curated multiphasic dataset of 132 multiparametric DCE-MRI scans from adult patients with chronic liver disease acquired on 1.5 T and 3 T MRI scanners between 2011 and 2020. The dataset includes both HCC-positive (n = 63) and HCC-negative (n = 69) patients, with up to five lesions per patient segmented across each sequence when confidently identified. Whole-liver and lesion segmentations were manually performed and expert-validated, with lesion metadata including LI-RADS scores, size, liver segment location, major LI-RADS imaging features (non-rim APHE, washout, capsule, threshold growth) and key ancillary/background findings (e.g., mosaic architecture, fat/blood products, necrosis, tumor-in-vein; cirrhosis and portal-hypertension signs). In total, 140 lesions were annotated, including 97 confirmed HCC. Additionally, we provide liver masks for all T1-weighted images (T1-WI) sequences, generated using a pre-trained nnU-Net model, as well as pre-computed transforms to facilitate registration across T1-WI phases. By providing a comprehensive, well-annotated, and standardized collection of liver MRI examinations, OpenSwissHCC aims to assist the development and benchmarking of advanced computational methods for automated HCC detection, segmentation, and characterization, fostering progress toward precision imaging and personalized treatment planning.

records.title: Head-to-head comparison of [18F]FAPI and [18F]FDG PET/CT in the clinical value of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: To investigate the clinical utility of fluorine-18-labeled fibroblast activation protein (FAP) inhibitor ([ 18 F]FAPI) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) relative to [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([ 18 F]FDG) PET/CT for tumor detection and staging in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. A cohort of 38 individuals (median age, 61 years; interquartile range, 56–68 years), all with pathologically confirmed primary or recurrent HCC, were enrolled. All participants underwent both [ 18 F]FDG and [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT. Maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), FAP expression tumor volume (FTV), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), total lesion FAP expression (TLF), and clinical staging were compared. Each patient had at least one intrahepatic lesion confirmed by surgical resection or percutaneous biopsy. Histopathologic confirmation was available for 46/66 intrahepatic lesions, 3/56 lymph-node (LN) metastases, and 4/33 distant metastases; the remaining lesions were adjudicated using a composite reference standard based on multimodal imaging follow-up and treatment response. Additionally, correlations between PET imaging findings and serum biomarkers, comprising alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist II (PIVKA-II), were analyzed. The cohort included 32 primary and 6 recurrent HCC cases. [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection rates than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic lesions (96.7% vs. 60.0%; p < 0.001), LN metastases (94.6% vs. 80.4%; p = 0.021), and distant metastases (78.8% vs. 48.5%; p = 0.002). For primary intrahepatic lesions, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.90 vs. 4.80, p < 0.001) and TBR (5.45 vs. 2.60, p < 0.001) than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT. In the patient-level volumetric analysis of the 32 initial-staging patients, FTV was 21.04 vs. MTV 13.75 ( p < 0.001), and TLF was 135.36 vs. TLG 51.44 ( p < 0.001). For LN metastases, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.98 vs. 6.63, p = 0.048) and TBR (7.85 vs. 4.95, p < 0.001), as well as higher FTV than MTV (6.55 vs. 4.55, p < 0.001) and TLF than TLG (67.65 vs. 52.75, p < 0.001). Positive correlations were observed between [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT tumor uptake parameters and AFP and PIVKA-II levels (nominal p < 0.05). Relative to [ 18 F]FDG, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT produced staging changes in 19/32 patients undergoing initial staging, including 6 true upstagings, and identified 3 additional local recurrences; a FAPI-informed management change was implemented in 57.9% (22/38) of patients. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.947, 0.921, 0.895, and 0.864 for SUVmax, TBR, FTV, and TLF, respectively. [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection in selected HCC settings than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic, lymph-node, and distant metastatic lesions and may provide complementary information for staging and treatment planning in this preliminary single-center cohort. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05810324; registered on 30 March 2023.

records.title: Foundation Model‐Enabled Pathology‐Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
records.abstract: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model-enabled framework for pathology-informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT-MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT-Clinical combines the PIVOT-MRI score with tumor size and alpha-fetoprotein. The multicenter retrospective study includes 2052 patients in a training cohort, an internal test cohort, and four external validation cohorts. PIVOT-MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839-0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT-Clinical increases the internal-test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT-Clinical-defined groups are associated with different two-year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation-related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT-MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis-related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology-defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI-only clinical inference pathway.

records.title: Combined analysis of preoperative circulating tumor cells status and tumor size to guide width of resection margin for solitary hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: Background The optimal resection margin width for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains controversial. The purpose of this study was to explore the value of preoperative circulating tumor cells (CTCs) status and tumor size in guiding the resection margin width of patients with HCC. Methods This study was a multicenter retrospective study that included 383 patients who underwent resection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Preoperative circulating tumor cell (CTC) detection (CTC ≥ 1/CTC = 0) and imaging evaluation of tumor size (≤ 3 cm/> 3 cm) were performed in all patients. We aimed to compare recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) between patients receiving narrow (< 1 cm) and wide (≥ 1 cm) resection margins. Results Tumor diameter and CTC status were independent predictors of RFS and OS in the entire cohort. In patients with tumor diameter ≤ 3 cm, CTC-positive status correlated with poorer RFS but not OS. RFS and OS of narrow margin group and wide margin group were similar, and there was no statistical significance (P > 0.05). In the patients with tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-negative group, the RFS and OS of the narrow margin group were comparable to those of the wide margin group (P > 0.05). However, in patients with tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-positive groups, RFS and OS were better in the wide margin group than in the narrow margin group (P < 0.05). Conclusions Using preoperative CTC status and tumor diameter as preoperative markers, combined analysis of CTC status and tumor diameter could help to determine surgical margin width in patients with solitary HCC. Narrow margins are indicated for patients with a tumor diameter ≤ 3 cm (regardless of CTC status) and for patients with a tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-negative. Whereas wide margins are preferred in patients with tumors > 3 cm in diameter and CTC-positive.

records.title: CT habitat and peritumoral radiomics for predicting progression after repeat TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter study
records.abstract: Background This study developed and validated an machine-learning-based radiomics model integrating tumor habitat radiomics, peritumoral radiomics, and clinical features to predict progression-free survival (PFS) following repeat transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 270 patients with HCC. Patients from Center 1 were assigned to training (n = 94) and internal validation (n = 41) cohorts, while Centers 2 (n = 82) and 3 (n = 53) served as external validation cohorts. Tumor habitats and 5-mm peritumoral regions were generated from contrast-enhanced CT images. Radiomics features were selected using univariate Cox and LASSO-Cox regression. A fusion model and HPC risk score were constructed by integrating selected radiomics signatures and clinical variables. Performance was assessed using time-dependent ROC, C-index, calibration, decision curve analysis, and Kaplan–Meier analyses. Results The optimal habitat cluster number was K = 2. Eleven habitat features, three peritumoral features, and alpha-fetoprotein were retained in the fusion model. The model achieved AUCs of 0.923, 0.921, and 0.897 for 3-, 6-, and 9-month progression-free survival in the training cohort, and 0.932, 0.863, and 0.916 in the internal validation cohort, respectively; all external AUCs exceeded 0.82. The fusion model showed higher C-index values than the clinical model across cohorts. High-risk patients had significantly shorter PFS than low-risk patients (all P < 0.001). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement and clinical utility. Conclusion The CT-based fusion model and HPC risk score effectively predicted progression risk in HCC.

records.title: Intratumoral habitat combined with peritumoral radiomics to improve the predictive performance of initial TACE efficacy: a multicenter retrospective study
records.abstract: Background and purpose Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) is the primary treatment for intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, significant heterogeneity in patient response to TACE necessitates non-invasive and precise methods for evaluating treatment efficacy. This study aims to explore the predictive ability of combined intratumoral habitat imaging and peritumoral radiomics features for TACE response. Materials and methods We retrospectively enrolled HCC patients who underwent TACE treatment at four centers between January 2015 and December 2023. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced MRI. Patients from centers A and B formed the training cohort, while those from centers C and D comprised external validation cohorts. Using three-phase enhanced MRI (arterial, portal venous, and delayed phase), K-Means clustering divided intratumoral regions into three habitat subregions (Habitat 1, 2, and 3), and peritumoral features were extracted. Clinical variables were also collected. Key radiomics features were selected by LASSO regression, and clinical indicators were identified through univariable and multivariable logistic regression. The XGBoost algorithm constructed intratumoral, peritumoral, clinical, and combined models. Performance was evaluated using ROC curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and DeLong tests. Results A total of 174 HCC patients who underwent initial TACE treatment were enrolled, including 104 in training and 70 in validation cohorts. Fifteen key intratumoral features from the habitat subregions and 24 radiomics features from the peritumoral region were identified, primarily derived from wavelet transforms and texture analysis. The wavelet-LLL_glszm_ZoneVariance_ PVP feature from Cluster 2 contributed significantly to the model and had a positive impact (highest SHAP value). Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (P = 0.015) and Tumor size (P = 0.016) remained significantly associated with TACE treatment response in multivariable analysis. The combined model based on clinical, intratumoral habitat and peritumoral radiomics showed superior predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.950 (95% CI: 0.89-1.00), 0.850 (0.79-0.91) and 0.830 (0.77-0.89) in training and validation cohorts, outperforming single models (Clinic: AUC = 0.700, Tumor_Habitat: AUC = 0.880, Peritumor_Radiomics: AUC = 0.870, P<0.05). Calibration and DCA demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes and favorable net benefit across the evaluated threshold probabilities. Conclusion The combined model integrating AFP, Tumor size, intratumoral habitat imaging, and peritumoral radiomics could accurately predict initial TACE response in HCC patients. Cluster 2-derived features showed relatively greater contributions among the intratumoral habitat subregions. This non-invasive prediction tool may provide complementary information for pretreatment risk stratification. Future prospective multicenter studies are needed to verify the clinical applicability of the model.
